label: sequence began with g: late original-phase steps and <DEL>
explanation: Fires when the first original token was g, from step 3 of the original phase through the <DEL> step. It does not depend on the current input token. It is silent at t=0..2 and essentially silent in the copy phase (64 activations in total). The ramp matters: activation is weak at t=3, about 0.2-0.3 of max, and grows to about 0.8-1.0 of max at middle original positions. Sequences that start with g g are among the strongest. Weak residual firing (under ~0.15 of max) happens when g is the second original token. This is the main source of missed activations: 3.4% of activation mass. Inactive false positives are mostly the t=3 step.

issues: Minor caveat: the main predicate's recall is 0.82 on test, and it covers only 33% of the lowest activation quartile. The missed steps (15.9k, 3.5% of mass) are almost all weak firings (0.01-0.21 of max) when orig(1)==g and t>=4. The explanation already says this. Only some sequences with g in second position fire: misses start with t, i, 2, p, q, while inactive cases start with c, z, h, v, x, 1, f. A predicate for this class alone gets precision 0.27 and F1 0.21. Adding (orig(1)==g)&(t>=5) to the predicate lowers test F1 to 0.852, which confirms why it was rejected.

Claims checked: copy phase has 64 activations in the dev split, and first_tok==g in the copy phase gets F1 0.0001. Rows that start with neither g nor g-second have precision 0.00015. Firing is zero at t=0..2. The ramp is real: first_tok==g at t==3 sits in the bottom quartiles (2.9% coverage in Q3, 0.1% in Q4), while orig_idx>=5 has precision 1.0 and covers 60% of the top quartile. Sequences starting g g are overrepresented in the top quartile (8.2% coverage vs 2.4% overall recall). All 1150 test false positives are at step 3 in the shown examples, which matches the claim.
The label matches the predicate and does not overclaim. Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.985, R 0.821, F1 0.895, mass recall 0.965.
